name: investment_fibo
description: Institutional Investment Relationship Ontology — translated 1:1 from the owner-supplied OWL (https://contextbuilder.ai/ontology/investment#, :InvestmentRelationshipOntology, 2026-08-11): all 12 owl:Class declarations become entity types and all 11 owl:ObjectProperty declarations become relations, with rdfs:domain/rdfs:range preserved exactly. v2.0 is a BREAKING rewrite of v1.1: the companion value types (MonetaryAmount/Date/Percentage/Identifier) and their carrier relations (hasValueAmount/hasFeeRate/effectiveOnDate/hasIdentifier) are REMOVED — they existed only because attribute values were previously unrepresentable, and are superseded by the datatype_properties declaration below (ADR-0008 amendment, spec v13). See _v13_dependency and _deviations_from_source_owl for what is inert until v13 ships and where this pack deliberately differs from the source OWL.
_v13_dependency: The `datatype_properties` array and the per-type `abstract` flag are declared here but are INERT until knowledge-graph spec v13 ships (KG-AC-69/70/72). Today's loader reads only entity_types/relations/regex_patterns/dep_patterns, so under v12 this pack yields 12 entity types + 11 relations and NO facts. The abstract types below will also fail to locate a span under v12 and be dropped — that is expected, and is precisely the gap v13 closes. Nothing here breaks the current loader (unknown keys are ignored).
_deviations_from_source_owl: TWO deliberate differences, both owner-approved: (1) `lei` is NOT declared. The source OWL declares iiro:lei on LegalEntity, but the owner directed at the v13 clarify pass (2026-08-11) that no LEI be carried — consistent in spirit with spec v11's removal of the gazetteer/external-identifier plane, even though the mechanism differs (v11 removed LOOKUP against an external index; this would have been TRANSCRIPTION of a value printed in the document). 15 of the source's 16 owl:DatatypeProperty declarations are translated. (2) The source OWL types every datatype property as xsd:string, INCLUDING dates and monetary amounts. Translating that faithfully would make `normalized_value` (KG-AC-70) a no-op and leave KG-AC-P11 unable to compare dates or amounts across documents, so the `range` kinds below are assigned SEMANTICALLY (date/number/identifier where the property clearly is one) rather than copying xsd:string uniformly. If the owner prefers literal fidelity to the OWL, set every range to `string` and accept that no normalisation occurs.
_known_gaps: The source OWL declares NO datatype properties for CommercialTerms, FeeSchedule, Amendment or SideLetter, and no `name` for InvestmentManager — so management/performance fees, billing frequency, settlement currency, amendment identifiers and their previous/new values, and side-letter provisions are NOT extractable under this pack even after v13. The owner's own extraction guide (§9) expects roughly 40 fields where the OWL declares 16. This is a SOURCE-ONTOLOGY gap, not a pack translation error — filling it requires the owner to extend the OWL. Also: no owl:subClassOf appears in the source, so every type below has `parent: null` and no subtype reasoning is available (domain/range checks are exact-match only).

entity_types.guidance: The overall institutional investment relationship between an investor and an investment manager — the central aggregate tying together the parties, the governing agreement and the subscriptions. ABSTRACT: a document never writes this as a literal phrase; name it after the parties it connects (e.g. "<Investor> - <Manager> Investment Relationship").

An institutional investor committing capital — a pension scheme, insurer, fund-of-funds, family office or similar named party. Conceptually aligned to FIBO Party. Often introduced with a defined term such as ("Investor"), ("Client") or ("Subscriber").
The investment management organisation appointed to manage assets — usually introduced with a defined term such as ("Investment Manager") or ("Manager").
The investment management agreement itself — the named contract document, usually carrying a reference number (e.g. IMA-2025-018) and a title such as INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT.
A fund subscription — the investor's commitment document for a specific fund, usually carrying its own reference (e.g. SUB-2025-041).
The named investment fund being subscribed into (a fund, sub-fund, feeder or named share class).

The capital commitment attached to a subscription — the undertaking itself, not the numeric amount (the amount, currency, date and type are datatype properties below). ABSTRACT: documents state the figures without naming the commitment as an entity; name it after what it commits (e.g. "<Amount> institutional subscription commitment").
The formally registered legal identity behind an investor — the registered legal name as it appears in onboarding/KYC material, as distinct from the trading or colloquial name.

The commercial arrangement governing an agreement — fees and related economics taken as a whole. ABSTRACT: documents describe the terms without naming them as an entity; name it after the agreement it belongs to (e.g. "Commercial Terms for <AgreementId>").
The named fee schedule document defining the commercial terms, usually carrying its own reference (e.g. FS-2025-031).
A formal amendment to an agreement — the named amending document (e.g. AMENDMENT NO. 1, reference AMD-2025-007).
A side letter supplementing an agreement with additional or investor-specific provisions, usually carrying its own reference (e.g. SL-2025-006).

relations.guidance: The investment relationship is with this investor.
The investment relationship appoints this investment manager.
The investment relationship is governed by this agreement.
The investment relationship includes this subscription.
The investor is backed by this formally incorporated legal entity.
The subscription invests into this named fund.
The subscription carries this capital commitment.
The agreement sets out these commercial terms.
The commercial terms are defined by this fee schedule.
The agreement is amended by this amendment.
The agreement is supplemented by this side letter.

datatype_properties.guidance: The agreement's reference number as printed (e.g. IMA-2025-018).
The kind of agreement (e.g. Investment Management Agreement).
The date the agreement takes effect.
The governing law / jurisdiction clause (e.g. laws of England and Wales).
How often the manager reports to the investor (e.g. Quarterly).
The subscription's reference number as printed (e.g. SUB-2025-041).
The committed capital figure (the currency is a separate property).
The date the capital commitment was made or becomes effective.
The kind of commitment (e.g. Institutional Commitment).
The registered legal name exactly as recorded.
The legal entity classification (e.g. Public Limited Company, Public Pension Trust).
The company/entity registration number as printed.
